key_insight: Data-informed random features provide a compact dictionary for learning continuous-time Koopman generators, improving on data-agnostic representations.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports efficient forecasting and interpretable analysis of nonlinear continuous-time systems learned from data.
method: Approximate the Koopman generator using Galerkin methods such as gEDMD.
Establish convergence of vector-field approximations and resulting trajectories.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments demonstrate accurate forecasting and system analysis with faster computation than iterative optimization, though the abstract provides no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: gEDMD does not generally preserve exponential boundedness, so stability of the learned evolution requires verification.
paper_title: Data-driven Random-feature Approximation of Koopman Generators of Nonlinear Continuous-time Systems
